subject: Sizing plan for Atlas Grid Dedicated deployment - burst & autoscale
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@atlasgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya.ramesh@atlasgrid.com>
Date: 2026-01-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial sizing ask - Dedicated + burst needs

Karthik,

Thanks again for the call this morning. To follow up: Atlas Grid is planning to move a critical inference workload to Redwood Dedicated in Q1. We expect a steady baseline (1.5k concurrent token streams) but have several weekly batch windows and nightly analytics jobs that spike to ~3x baseline for 45-120 minutes.

Key asks:
- Can you describe your recommended reservation vs burst split for a deal of this size?
- What autoscale triggers do you recommend to avoid cold starts but also limit cost?
- How do fallbacks work if Dedicated capacity is saturated — automatic routing to hosted or degraded model variant?

Attached is a rough estimate of our usage (atlas_estimated_q1_usage.csv). Looking to get a concise proposal we can review with procurement next week.

Best,
Samir
Director of ML Platforms
Atlas Grid

Attachments:
- atlas_estimated_q1_usage.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@atlasgrid.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-12T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask - Dedicated + burst needs

Samir — thanks for the details and the file, that helps. High-level proposal below; attaching a one-page sketch (redwood_proposed_capacity.pdf) for the deal.

Summary recommendation (baseline deal size ~1.5k concurrent):
- Reserve: 100% of 1.5k baseline as Dedicated slab (guaranteed pods) to meet SLO for 99th pct latency.
- Elastic buffer (soft headroom): additional 40% kept warm across the same pool for small-to-medium spikes (continuous batching + KV prefix cache preserved).
- Burst pool: configurable preemptible instances (up to 2.5x baseline) to accommodate large spikes for short windows. These are lower-cost, may have slightly higher cold-start risk unless proactively warmed.

Autoscale policy (suggested):
- Scale up triggers: sustained queue_length > 60s for 30s OR GPU_util > 65% for 45s OR token_throughput > 1.7x baseline for 60s.
- Scale down: conservative decay (keep warm for 15–30 minutes) to prevent oscillation during rolling spikes.
- Canary/warmup: when burst action is triggered for >10 minutes, spin a warmup batch to pre-load KV caches to reduce tail latency.

Fallbacks and graceful degradation:
- Primary: automatic routing to compatible model variant in same region with slightly lower compute (quantized variant) to preserve correctness with a modest latency uplift.
- Secondary: cross-region fallback to hosted Redwood API (policy-managed, only if customer allows) with token routing and audit logs.

Cost controls:
- Meter burst usage separately; add soft quotas and notifications at 70/90% of burst budget.
- Option: committed cushion (monthly headroom commit) at discounted rate to reduce overage surprises.

Next steps: I can convert this into an MPL (mutual plan + pricing) and draft the autoscale knobs we’ll configure in the Dedicated console. Looping Neha for procurement/terms and Laura for SRE/ops concerns.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Field Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments:
- redwood_proposed_capacity.pdf (pdf, 1 page)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@atlasgrid.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-13T08:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask - Dedicated + burst needs

Samir — quick procurement/compliance notes that will affect the sizing agreement and billing cadence: 

- If Atlas requires Private (VPC) deployment with KMS-backed keys, we need to size for slightly more baseline headroom because cross-node cache warming is slower in air-gapped setups. Recommend an extra 10% baseline cushion in that case.
- For regulated log retention (90d vs default 30d) we’ll need to include longer telemetry retention which increases cost by ~3–5% on observability storage.
- We can include a capped overage credit for the first quarter of the contract (e.g., first 10% burst overage credit) as a one-time concession for the onboarding period — if procurement approves.

Attaching SLA comparison table for quick reference.

-Neha
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
Attachments:
- sla-ratings.pdf (pdf, 2 pages)

From: Samir Shah <samir@atlasgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya.ramesh@atlasgrid.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-14T10:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask - Dedicated + burst needs

Karthik / Neha — this is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and infra: 

- Can you put the recommended knobs into a Mutual Action Plan we can circulate (timelines, checkpoints, runbook handoff)?
- For the preemptible burst pool: what is the expected tail-latency penalty (p95/p99) for quantized variant vs full-res model when routed automatically? Any ballpark numbers help procurement approve.
- Would Redwood entertain a short-term overage credit (first 90 days) for spikes that exceed burst pool while we tune autoscale? That would materially reduce our risk.

Also looping Priya (infra lead) to flag region constraints — we need capacity in us-west and avoid cross-region fallbacks unless explicitly approved.

Thanks — can we target a short review call on Friday?

—Samir

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Priya Ramesh <priya.ramesh@atlasgrid.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask - Dedicated + burst needs

Samir / Priya — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short runbook excerpt in the Drive link below. Key bullets and next steps: 

- MAP highlights: baseline reservation = 1.5k concurrent; warm buffer = 40% baseline; burst cap = 2.5x baseline (preemptible). Pricing options: monthly cushion commit (10%/20% tiers) vs pay-go burst.
- Tail-latency: expected p95 uplift for quantized variant ~ +30–70ms, p99 uplift can be larger during first-minute cold-starts (we mitigate with warmup batches). We’ll include measured numbers in the MAP appendix based on a short canary run.
- Overage credit: Redwood can offer a one-time overage credit covering the first 10% of burst overage for Q1 onboarding (subject to signed SOW).
- Region constraint: we will not enable cross-region fallback without explicit sign-off; primary and warm buffer will be provisioned in us-west.

Suggested timeline:
1) Friday: 30m review call to walk MAP and pricing (I’ll send calendar invite).
2) Week 1 post-sign: run a 48-hour canary (production-shaped traffic) to measure tail and warmup behavior.
3) Week 2: finalize knobs and lock the reserved slab + burst cap.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_example_playbooks
HubSpot: HS-DEAL-4821

I’ll send the calendar invite for Friday morning PST. Thanks all — happy to iterate on the MAP doc prior to the call.

—Karthik
Head of Field Solutions — Redwood Inference
